claim_retracted: That the phase-field relaxation visibly curved the grain boundaries.
measurement: Relabelled each relaxed grain onto its majority Voronoi ancestor, so a changed cell means the BOUNDARY moved rather than a label being reassigned, then counted changed cells and divided the changed area by the Voronoi boundary length to get a mean displacement.
reading: The boundaries moved 0.2-0.3% of a grain width, 2-3% of the diffuse interface width, and under a tenth of one grid cell. They did not move. Six times the horizon (0.25 to 1.5 grain times) bought ONE additional changed cell at n=16, which is consistent with the mobility being inert.
consequence_for_the_junction_numbers: This puts a caveat on the junction-spread improvement I reported for the phase-field route (31.8 -> 25.4 degrees at n=16). With ~30 junctions and 49 changed cells, that is about 1.6 cells per junction -- and changed cells concentrate at junctions, where curvature is highest. A sub-cell change in the diffuse field can rotate a measured boundary TANGENT without the boundary migrating. So that improvement is plausibly a sub-cell labelling effect at the junctions rather than relaxation, and it should not be read as the phase-field route partially working.
unaffected: The threshold-dynamics route moves boundaries by construction (the argmax of a diffused indicator), and its boundary length falls monotonically by 2-7%, so its morphology change is real. Its numbers stand.
